description: A utilities manager must decide whether to conditionally authorize Line 4's newly installed closed-loop rinse system before a municipal water restriction begins and finalize the operating and discharge controls, with input from process engineering and environmental compliance.

shared_context.S1: Line 4 currently uses fresh rinse water during each production shift.
shared_context.S2: A municipal water-conservation restriction begins on Monday and will limit nonessential fresh-water use at the plant.
shared_context.S3: A closed-loop rinse-recovery skid has been installed beside Line 4 but has not yet been placed into production service.
shared_context.S4: Mara makes the final utilities authorization and operating-control decision.
shared_context.S5: The plant's Monday pre-run huddle routinely reviews process and environmental constraints before a new utility system is placed into service.
shared_context.S6: Plant utility policy allows a system to receive conditional authorization in the pre-run huddle when pending engineering or compliance paperwork is recorded as a required pre-start commitment; conditional authorization means the system may proceed once those commitments are completed.
shared_context.S7: The Monday pre-run huddle includes a technical review in which process engineering and environmental compliance report applicable operating and discharge requirements.
shared_context.S8: When settling, Mara records the fact IDs for technical findings used in the decision and records each required pre-start commitment as a separate commitment.
shared_context.S9: The huddle agenda reserves separate report slots for process engineering and environmental compliance before Mara settles the authorization and controls.

PF1.text: Eli's commissioning trial found that loop conductivity reaches 1,200 microsiemens per centimeter after 40 cycles, while Line 4's rinse specification allows no more than 900; the validated operating plan is to purge exactly 300 liters every 30 cycles. The skid vendor also confirmed that pump-seal replacement and recommissioning require exactly 6 hours, but Eli's trial worksheet is still awaiting engineering signoff.

PF2.text: Nadia's permit review, confirmed with the regulator yesterday, requires every recovery-loop purge to be neutralized to a pH from exactly 7.13 through 7.47, with a sample collected during the first 90 seconds of each purge before discharge and an entry made for every purge in the wastewater log; she has not attached the regulator's note to the utility change record yet.

acceptance_conditions: The closed-loop rinse system must receive conditional authorization for Line 4.
The system must purge exactly 300 liters every 30 cycles.
The plan must reserve exactly 6 hours for pump-seal replacement and recommissioning.
Every purge must be controlled to a pH range of exactly 7.13 through 7.47.
A sample must be required during the first 90 seconds of every purge before discharge.
An entry for every purge must be required in the wastewater log.
The pending engineering signoff and regulator-note attachment must be recorded as separate pre-start commitments.

content_checks.C7: any(c['target'] == 'Eli' and 'engineering' in c['detail'] and 'signoff' in c['detail'] for c in commitments) and any(c['target'] == 'Nadia' and 'regulator' in c['detail'] and 'note' in c['detail'] and 'utility change record' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: Eli's trial changes the operating plan to exactly 300 liters every 30 cycles, the vendor assessment changes reserved downtime to exactly 6 hours, and the pending trial worksheet creates the engineering-signoff commitment.

Nadia's regulator-confirmed review changes the pH limits to exactly 7.13 and 7.47, requires sampling during the first 90 seconds and wastewater-log entry for every purge, and creates the regulator-note attachment commitment.
